newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing - electronic money not harming policy.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing - electronic money not harming policy.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday that innovations in electronic payments were not infringing on the German central bank's monetary policy.

In the text of a speech to be delivered to a payments conference, Issing said developments in M3 money supply, the Bundesbank's top policy indicator, had not been affected by the expansion in electronic payment options.
"The volatility of M3 money supply has increased in the nineties. However this primarily reflects interest rate developments and money capital formation," Issing said.
"Innovations in payments do not put in question the Bundesbank's monopoly on central bank money."
At the same time, Issing said there would be a "significant increase" in electronic money in the medium and long term.
"We will watch the developments very carefully, but in accordance with experience and analysis so far, in a very relaxed manner," Issing said.
